A reading of the design, not a departure (for REVIEWER and ORCH): 4.6 says labels.js «places every label only through the custom properties of the stage element (below)», and gives it moveYou(x); 4.6 view.js, 4.10 («--you (in office/view.js)») and the look's 5.2 (d) («from app/public/office/view.js and app/public/js/pages/demo.js») put every CSSOM write in view.js. Read together: labels.js writes no style at all — the style sheet places each label from the stage's custom properties, which only view.js writes (the --you write per frame of a walk moves the «Вы» label with the figure) — and moveYou(x) is the label module's part of a move that is not a style write: when «Вы» comes to stand at x (the first frame, the last frame of a walk, a placement at once), the place line #stage-you says the door or the desk of x (you_at_door, you_at_desk); an x that is no place changes nothing. So PP-6 can read nine literal setProperty names in view.js and no .style in labels.js. If ORCH reads 4.6 the other way (labels.js writing --you), that would contradict 4.10 and the look's 5.2 (d), and is a question for CODE-DESIGNER.

How the text list gets its words (no departure; the interfaces of 4.6 leave it open): the scene's words (buildScene keeps exactly stages, roles, you, doorName, doorTagline) do not hold the lines desk_line, you_at_door and you_at_desk that 4.6 and 4.3 make labels.js write, and createLabels gets no words. So labels.js imports TEXTS of ../shared/i18n/texts.js and writes those three keys in the language the page has set on its root element (doc.documentElement.lang, which applyTexts sets), with the Russian value for a language the module lacks; the words of the sign, the «Вы» label and the plates stay the scene's. A contract for rows F6 and F7 (landing.js, demo.js): call applyTexts before mountStage and, on a language switch, before stage.setWords (else the text list keeps the earlier language until the next render), and mountTheme before mountStage (mountTheme sets data-theme at mount without onChange, and the first frame reads the palette of the theme drawn); on a theme change call stage.refresh("theme") from mountTheme's onChange; the size is followed by view.js itself. The design's 4.5 already names this order (applyTexts; mountLangSwitch; mountTheme; mountStage).

Choices inside what the design leaves open, each serving a rule of 4.6, for REVIEWER and TEST-DESIGNER: (a) a «size change» is a change of the stage's geometry: a resize that changes it places «Вы» at the target of the state taken at once (a new walker on the new stage map), the camera at its offset at once, writes the custom properties, the canvas size and data-figure, and draws one frame; a resize that leaves the geometry as it was (for example a height inside the same H) draws nothing and a walk goes on; (b) refresh("theme") reads the palette once and draws one frame, refresh("lang") renders the labels again and draws one frame, refresh("size") is a resize, any other reason does nothing; setWords draws one frame (words that buildScene refuses are ignored); changes before the next frame share one frame, and a change during a walk is drawn by the walk's next frame; (c) a tap whose state differs but whose place is where the walk goes already (the result while walking to desk 4) adds no frame: the walk's frames draw the new state; (d) the 40 ms rule counts from the last frame drawn of any kind, so a walk's first frame waits up to 40 ms after a load or a one-off frame; the time step of a walk frame is min(now − last step, 100) ms; the last frame of a walk sets the camera to its target exactly; the camera of a redirect eases from the offset drawn at the tap over min(700, the new walk's distance / 72 s); (e) the text view is final for every failure (getContext null, drawScene throwing, no geometry, no stage map, the load state or words refused at the start); taps, words and a language refresh still update the text list there when a geometry is known; (f) reduced motion turned on during a walk places «Вы» at the target at once with one frame; (g) the place line is written when «Вы» stands, so during a walk it keeps the place «Вы» left and names the target after the walk (criterion 6: «the text list says it after the walk»); the plates' now, the light and the poses change with the walk's first frame (the look's 10); (h) data-frames is "0" from the mount, data-figure 22 · s from the first frame; both by setAttribute; (i) mountStage trims the computed token values before readPalette (Chrome 157 gives them trimmed already, F4's I7 (d)) and takes s as parseInt of the computed --px; the theme drawn is themeFor(readChoice(data-theme), the system's dark) of js/theme.js, the rule tokens.css follows; (j) createWalker gets speed 72 and frameMs 160 explicitly (its defaults, the look's 9.8), so the camera's walk time uses the same number; (k) the label elements are made at the first render and updated in place, so a plate keeps the look's .3 s background and colour transition when it becomes current; the plate lines split at the first space (U+0020), so a no-break space keeps two words on one line.

labels.say(text) is built as 4.6 names it (it writes the live region #live, given to createLabels), but nothing in this row calls it: the StageView of 4.6 is { tap, setWords, refresh } and exposes no say, and 4.3 gives the live region to the page scripts (landing.js says live_desk on how, 4.5; demo.js its answers). If F6 or F7 should announce through the labels, that needs the StageView to carry say — a question for CODE-DESIGNER through ORCH, not taken here; until then the page scripts write #live themselves by textContent.

The hidden page is proved by the driver (OV-3 and its neighbours, and four hidden mutants each red), not live: headless Chrome 157.0.8103.80 keeps document.visibilityState «visible» for a page behind another page and for a minimized window (self_check «HIDDEN live»). REQ-112 criterion 7 gives the live check to UAT-RUNNER in a real Chrome (data-frames does not grow while the tab is hidden).

For TEST-DESIGNER (T3, OV-1 … OV-7; T4, ST-1 … ST-6): the stand-in surface view.js uses — canvas { width, height, getContext("2d") }; stage { style.setProperty(name, value), setAttribute(name, value), classList.add(name), scrollLeft (written) }; labels { render(scene, geom), moveYou(x) }; deps now, raf, caf, matchMedia (a list with matches and addEventListener("change", fn) or addListener(fn)), hidden, onVisibility, onResize, token, px, viewport, theme. A test ticking every 16 ms sees a walk's first frame on the third tick after a frame (the 40 ms rule); OV-7's size change must change the geometry (I10 (a)); the first frame is drawn inside createStageView unless hidden() is true. The design's mutants M55–M59 and the two mutants decisions/0124 H4 names for ST-5 (the drawScene exception escapes; a null context gets no text-view class) are red in the driver of this step (self_check «MUTANTS»), which can serve as a map; the tests themselves are T3's and T4's. In the browser, ST-2's loop reads the stage's --you from getComputedStyle (an inline custom property), and the place line names the target only after the walk (I10 (g)).

A named limit of the text view: when no geometry can be computed (the computed --px not 2, 3 or 4, or a viewport size that is not a whole number from 1), labels.render gets no scene and the text list keeps the static Russian lines of the page; on a page in kk or en that window shows Russian lines. With the style sheet loaded --px is always 2, 3 or 4, so this is a page without its style sheet. A room over 2 000 logical px (no stage map) has a geometry, and there the text list is written in the page's language (measured in the driver).
